questions.prompt: A scientist who studies living organisms is called a:
questions.explanation: A biologist is a scientist who studies life and living organisms.

questions.prompt: A scientist's experiment gives results that do NOT match the prediction of their hypothesis. What should the scientist do?
options: Hide the results and keep the hypothesis
Accept that the hypothesis may be wrong and rethink it
Change the results to fit the hypothesis
questions.explanation: If results do not support a hypothesis, an honest scientist treats the hypothesis as possibly wrong and revises or replaces it.

questions.prompt: Dr Gebissa Ejeta is famous for improving which Ethiopian crop to resist drought and the Striga weed?
questions.explanation: Dr Gebissa Ejeta developed sorghum varieties that resist drought and the parasitic Striga weed.

questions.prompt: Scientists share their tested research with others by publishing it in a:
questions.explanation: Scientists publish their research in journals so other experts can read and check the work.

questions.prompt: Dr Melaku Worede is best known internationally for his work in:
options: Saving and conserving the genetic diversity of crops
questions.explanation: Dr Melaku Worede led work to collect and conserve the genetic diversity of Ethiopia's crops in a seed bank.

questions.prompt: Apart from being cheap, why is Endod (soapberry) a good choice for controlling disease-carrying snails in rural areas?
options: It is poisonous to all fish and plants
It is locally available and breaks down naturally in the water
It must be imported from abroad
It only works inside a laboratory
questions.explanation: Endod grows locally and breaks down naturally in a couple of days, so it is affordable and environmentally friendly.

questions.prompt: Which part of the cell controls what substances enter and leave it?
questions.explanation: The cell membrane controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell.

questions.prompt: The spreading of particles from where there are many of them to where there are fewer is called:
questions.explanation: Diffusion is the movement of particles from a region of high concentration to a region of low concentration.

questions.prompt: What is the job of the chloroplast in a plant cell?
options: To trap sunlight and make food
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which traps sunlight so the plant can make food by photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: A plant cell that is full of water and firm is described as:
questions.explanation: A turgid cell is swollen and firm because it is full of water, which helps keep the plant upright.

questions.prompt: Why can an electron microscope show much finer detail than a light microscope?
questions.explanation: The electron microscope has far higher resolution, so it can tell two very close points apart and show finer detail.

questions.prompt: A plant cell is placed in very salty water and its contents shrink away from the cell wall. This happened because water:
options: Moved into the cell by osmosis
Moved out of the cell by osmosis
Was made by the cell wall
questions.explanation: In salty water there is less water outside the cell, so water leaves the cell by osmosis, causing the contents to shrink (plasmolysis).

questions.prompt: Which part of the body begins digestion by breaking food into small pieces?
questions.explanation: Teeth in the mouth break food into smaller pieces, which is the start of digestion.

questions.prompt: Injera made from teff is mainly a source of which nutrient that gives the body energy?
questions.explanation: Injera made from teff is rich in carbohydrate, which is the body's main source of energy.

questions.prompt: What is the main job of red blood cells?
options: To carry oxygen around the body
questions.explanation: Red blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs to all parts of the body.

questions.prompt: In the alveoli of the lungs, which gas passes from the air into the blood?
questions.explanation: Oxygen passes from the air in the alveoli into the blood, while carbon dioxide passes from the blood into the air to be breathed out.

questions.prompt: If the body could not make digestive enzymes, what would most likely happen?
options: Food would be broken down faster
Large food molecules could not be broken down for absorption
More oxygen would enter the blood
questions.explanation: Enzymes speed up the breakdown of large food molecules into small ones; without them, food could not be digested and absorbed properly.

questions.prompt: Which of these micro-organisms is a fungus?
questions.explanation: Yeast is a fungus used to make dough rise. The others are a virus, a protozoan, and a bacterium.

questions.prompt: Which action best helps prevent the spread of infectious diseases?
options: Washing hands and using clean water
questions.explanation: Good hygiene such as washing hands and using clean water helps stop germs from spreading.

questions.prompt: Why does a person with untreated AIDS easily catch other infections?
options: Their immune system has become very weak
They have too many red blood cells
questions.explanation: HIV damages the immune system, so in AIDS the body can no longer fight off infections that a healthy body would resist.

questions.prompt: Which is the smallest group used when classifying living things?
questions.explanation: The species is the smallest classification group; members of a species can breed to produce fertile offspring.

questions.prompt: Which set of features best describes organisms in the Animal kingdom?
options: Many-celled, make their own food, do not move
Many-celled, cannot make their own food, usually move
questions.explanation: Animals are many-celled organisms that cannot make their own food and usually move from place to place to find it.

questions.prompt: An animal that eats only plants is called a:
questions.explanation: A herbivore is an animal that feeds only on plants, such as a cow or a gazelle.

questions.prompt: In the food chain grass to gazelle to cheetah, what is most likely to happen to the cheetahs if all the gazelles die from disease?
options: The cheetahs will increase in number
The cheetahs will have less food and decrease
Nothing will change for the cheetahs
questions.explanation: Cheetahs depend on gazelles for food, so if the gazelles die the cheetahs lose their food source and their numbers fall.
